To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Yang–Mills theory can be formulated as a general relativistic theory of a tetrad field, the Yang–MILLS theory can be formulated in terms of the tetrad field, and the Yang–MILL theory can be formulated using the metric tensor.
the Yang–Mills theory can be reformulated in the language of gravity.

the QCD Lagrangians can be represented as a sum of two Lagrangians: the usual Lagrangian of general relativity with tetrad fields and matter and some other additional fields where these tetrad fields and metric are constructed from the initial SU(3)-Yang–Mills fields.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Is it possible to construct the Lagrangian that contains only the Yang–Mills field, which would be equivalent to the standard QCD?
the possibility of reformulating the QCD Lagrangians in the language of the general relativity.
the following questions: (i) Is it possible to represent the QCD Lagrangians in the language of the Einstein theory?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Yang–Mills theory is a theory of gravity and the Yang–Milton equations are equations of motion for the gravitational field.
QCD can be reformulated in the language of the Einstein general relativity.
QCD Lagrangians are the Lagrangians of Einstein–Cartan–Sciama–Kibble gravity theory with the tetrad field constructed from the Yang–Mills field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a way to reformulate Yang–Mills theory in a form where the metric and tetrad fields are not independent but constructed from Yang–Mills field.
the Yang–Mills field is not a gauge field but a gravitational field.
the Yang–Mills theory is a special case of general relativity, which is formulated in the space of the tetrad fields.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the standard Lagrangian of QCD can be represented as a sum of the Lagrangian describing the gravitational field and the Lagrangians of matter and some new fields.
the tetrad fields in the reformulated Lagrangian are determined by the initial Yang–Mills field strength and the tetrad fields are not independent variables.
Yang–Mills theory is a theory of the tetrad field and the metric.
